params.body:
The monitor counted refusals over the last day and raised "nu" at 50. A Claude login that was refused a few hundred times and then repaired kept the wall red for up to a day after the fix, because the window only forgets a refusal once it is 24 hours old. A siren that stays on after the repair teaches the reader to stop looking.

## What changes

- `measure()` now also reports `refusals.quietMinutes`: minutes since the last refusal in the window.
- `assess()`: once a day's count reaches the weekly threshold but nothing has been refused for `THRESHOLDS.refusalsQuietMinutes` (60), it files one background finding, "An outside party refused us, and has stopped". The finding carries the count, the top group and how long ago the last refusal came. A stream that is still running keeps its "nu" / "deze week" severity as before.
- A reading without `quietMinutes` (an older caller) behaves as before.

## Tests

- `test/monitor.test.mjs`: a stream that is still running is "nu", the same count gone quiet for 10 hours is background with a calm verdict, and the measurement reports 0 quiet minutes for a refusal just written.
- Full suite: 1167 pass, 6 fail. The 6 are the report-render tests, which need `pdftoppm`; the workbench does not have it.
params.title: A refusal stream that has stopped is background, not a siren
